name: Amalek
overview: Amalek was a male Edomite chief, distinguished as the son of Eliphaz. He is noted in Scripture as a significant figure within the Edomite lineage, and his descendants became known as the Amalekites, a notable group mentioned in the Bible. His leadership role and tribal affiliation highlight his importance in the genealogical records of Edom.
namesAndTitles: The name Amalek appears as a proper name in Scripture without a given meaning or divine origin. It is simply recorded as the name of this Edomite chief in Genesis 36:12, reflecting a straightforward personal designation.
familyAndRelationships: Amalek is identified as the son of Eliphaz and Timna, situating him within a notable Edomite family line. Additionally, he is considered an ancestor of Agag, linking him to later biblical figures. Scripture thus records a clear lineage connecting him to significant descendants.
scriptureSignificance: Amalek's significance lies in his role as the progenitor of the Amalekites, a group that appears in biblical history. As a chief of Edom and son of Eliphaz, he represents a key ancestral figure, establishing a lineage that influences later events and interactions with Israel. His mention underscores the continuity of God's providential plan through various tribal histories.
